---
title: "3 PCR Product Check by Agarose Gel Electrophoresis"
---

**Approximate time:** 2 hours

## Material

### Equipment and tools

- Electrophoresis box with power supply
- Gel casting tray and comb
- Microwave-safe flask or beaker
- UV transilluminator or gel imaging system
- Balance
- Microwave
- 20 µL pipette
- Camera or smartphone

### Consumables and reagents

- Gloves, paper towels, Parafilm
- 20 µL tips
- 1× TAE buffer
- Agarose powder
- DNA stain such as GelRed
- Molecular-weight marker / DNA ladder
- DNA loading dye
- PCR product

## Instructions

- [ ] Weigh 1 g agarose for 100 mL 1× TAE buffer (1% gel unless the workshop lead specifies another concentration).
- [ ] Dissolve agarose carefully in a microwave-safe vessel.
- [ ] Cool slightly and add the selected DNA stain according to its instructions.
- [ ] Pour the gel, insert comb and allow the gel to solidify.
- [ ] Place the gel in the electrophoresis chamber and cover with 1× TAE.
- [ ] Load the selected molecular-weight marker.
- [ ] Mix an aliquot of PCR product with loading dye and load the samples.
- [ ] Include negative and positive controls where available.
- [ ] Run under the workshop-defined voltage/time (the WAMBAnet reference used 120 V for ~30 min).
- [ ] Visualize and document bands.
- [ ] Compare band size with the **expected product for the primer pair actually used**.
- [ ] Record non-specific bands, smear, weak product or no product.

::: {.callout-important}
The long reference-PCR sizes are not yet universal fixed values. A band should therefore be judged against the species-specific in-silico prediction recorded in Chapter 1, not against an invented single size.
:::
